name: Thrombocytopenia with Absent Radius Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for TAR Syndrome

criteria.description: Bilateral absence of the radius bone confirmed by radiographic imaging
Persistent thrombocytopenia with platelet counts typically below 50,000/µL in infancy
Presence of both thumbs despite absent radius
Identification of compound heterozygous mutations or deletions involving RBM8A gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of bilateral absent radius with thrombocytopenia and presence of thumbs
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory; absence of radius with thrombocytopenia and thumbs differentiates TAR from other radial aplasia syndromes.

searchTerms: missing radius bone in both arms
very low platelet count in infancy

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of bilateral thumbs despite absent radius
searchTerms: both thumbs present despite missing radius
thumbs present with absent forearm bone

common.symptomName: Petechiae and bruising due to thrombocytopenia
searchTerms: small red or purple skin spots
bruising and petechiae from low platelets

common.symptomName: Upper limb deformities including short forearms
searchTerms: upper limb abnormalities with short forearms
temporary low blood calcium after birth
low calcium levels in newborn period
heart defects like atrial septal defect
renal swelling due to urine buildup

occasional.symptomName: Recurrent infections due to transient immunodeficiency
searchTerms: frequent infections from temporary immune weakness
recurrent infections due to transient immunodeficiency
infections caused by short-term immune problems

rare.symptomName: Gastrointestinal malformations such as cow’s milk intolerance
Skeletal anomalies beyond radius absence (e.g. lower limb abnormalities)

laboratory: Marked thrombocytopenia (platelet count often <50,000/µL) in infancy
Normal to mildly decreased white blood cell counts
imaging: Radiographs showing bilateral absence of radius bones with presence of thumbs
genetic: Compound heterozygous mutations or deletions involving RBM8A gene on chromosome 1q21.1
other: Clinical observation of petechiae and bruising
Feeding assessment for intolerance or difficulties

distinguishingFeatures: Absent thumbs (unlike TAR where thumbs are present)
Cardiac septal defects with upper limb malformations
Presence of radius but hypoplastic or absent thumbs

redFlags: Severe thrombocytopenia with bleeding risk in neonate
Bilateral absent radius with preserved thumbs
Recurrent bleeding episodes or petechiae in infancy
references: Boussion S, et al. TAR syndrome: clinical and genetic update. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2020.
Albers CA, et al. Compound inheritance of a low-frequency regulatory SNP and a rare null mutation in RBM8A causes TAR syndrome. Nat Genet. 2012.
Orphanet: Thrombocytopenia with absent radius syndrome. Orphanet Report Series. 2021.
